```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = '#>', message = FALSE)
```

A generated wrapper can call the right helper and still return the wrong result
or throw afterward. Fixed contract tests check successful completion, exact
helper arguments, call order/count, and the final result. Write expectations
from the reviewed API/helper contract, independently of generated wrapper text.

This standalone example creates a temporary client and runs its generated test
offline. Install `httr2` and `testthat` first if they are not available.

## 1. Prepare a client with one selected operation

```{r client}
schema <- system.file('catalogue/schema.json', package = 'specmill', mustWork = TRUE)
root <- tempfile('tested-client-')
created <- specmill::initialize_client(
  root, schema, package = 'testedclient', title = 'Tested Catalogue Client',
  author = list(given = 'Example', family = 'Maintainer', email = 'you@example.org'),
  license = 'MIT + file LICENSE', base_url = 'https://api.example.org'
)
service_path <- file.path(root, 'apis/default.yml')
service <- yaml::read_yaml(service_path)
service$schemas$files <- as.list(service$schemas$files)
service$selection <- list(include = list('GET /items/{item_id}'))
yaml::write_yaml(service, service_path)
```

For your real client, use its existing root and selection policy. Do not narrow
selection simply to hide missing tests. Here the teaching client intentionally
has just `get_item()`.

## 2. Save independent fixed expectations

An RDS contract preserves R types and classes. `calls` is an ordered sequence;
each entry contains a helper name, its expected arguments, and its mock response.

```{r fixture}
contracts <- list(
  get_item = list(
    inputs = list(item_id = 'item-1', language = 'en'),
    calls = list(list(
      helper = 'api_request',
      arguments = list(
        method = 'GET', path = '/items/{item_id}',
        path_params = list(item_id = 'item-1'),
        query = list(language = 'en'), body = NULL,
        request_controls = list(timeout = 30L, max_retries = 0L, retry_writes = FALSE),
        server = list(diagnostic = 'Relative server URL requires a recorded origin or explicit base URL override')
      ),
      response = list(id = 'item-1', title = 'Example item')
    )),
    result = list(id = 'item-1', title = 'Example item')
  )
)
fixture <- file.path(root, 'tests/testthat/fixtures/contracts.rds')
dir.create(dirname(fixture), recursive = TRUE)
saveRDS(contracts, fixture)
cat('\ncontracts_file: tests/testthat/fixtures/contracts.rds\n',
    file = file.path(root, 'apis/default.yml'), append = TRUE)
```

Keys such as `get_item` are public wrapper names.

`contracts_file` may instead be a readable `.yml`, `.yaml` or `.json` file under
`tests/testthat/`, keyed by `METHOD /path` (for example `GET /items/{item_id}`).
Route keys survive renaming a wrapper and give reviewable diffs. Text fixtures
cannot tell `1L` from `1`, so their generated tests compare with
`expect_equal()`; use RDS when exact types matter. Add `yaml` to the client's
`Suggests`, as the generated tests read the file with it. A key naming both a
wrapper and its route is an error. Inputs use their public R names.
Specify types intentionally: `1L` is an integer, `1` is a double, and exact
expectations distinguish them. Use actual response classes (for example tibbles)
when preserving an existing client. Never put credentials in fixtures.

Optional contract `environment` values are scoped environment variables for the
test, implemented with `withr::local_envvar()`. Add `withr` to that client's test
dependencies if using this field. Keep environment values nonsecret.

## 3. Add the standard package test runner

Initialization declares testthat in `Suggests` but does not create its runner.
For this new client, create `tests/testthat.R`:

```{r runner}
writeLines(c(
  'library(testthat)', 'library(testedclient)', "test_check('testedclient')"
), file.path(root, 'tests/testthat.R'))
```

Use your own package name. Existing packages should keep their current runner
and manual tests.

## 4. Generate and run the test

```{r generate}
# Offline fixture only; real schemas use the required validation gate.
plan <- specmill::generate_client(validation = FALSE, root, config = 'specmill.yml', mode = 'plan')
stopifnot(!length(plan$diagnostics), length(plan$operations) == 1L)
applied <- specmill::generate_client(validation = FALSE, root, config = 'specmill.yml', mode = 'apply')
checked <- specmill::generate_client(validation = FALSE, root, config = 'specmill.yml', mode = 'check')
stopifnot(file.exists(file.path(root, 'tests/testthat/test-contract-get_item.R')))
```

The fixed sequence test reads the RDS fixture and replaces `api_request` in the
client namespace with a recorder. The placeholder URL is never contacted.

```{r run-tests}
testthat::test_local(root, filter = 'contract-get_item', stop_on_failure = TRUE)
```

Use `stop_on_failure = TRUE` in automation. Merely exiting R successfully is not
enough if a test command only prints failures. In a larger client, also run the
existing bespoke tests for the helpers and hooks you changed.

## 5. Inspect test coverage separately from execution

```{r coverage}
inspection <- specmill::inspect_client(root)
inspection$coverage
stopifnot(inspection$coverage$testedclient$contracts == 1L)
```

`implemented` counts selected named exports with source definitions. `contracts`
counts fixed contract declarations with generated test files. Neither count says
tests passed. Unsupported selected operations stay in the coverage denominator;
manual exports are reported separately.

`generation_command(root, kind = 'tests', args = '--check')` also requires fixed
contracts for all selected operations. Its `--dry-run` mode can show gaps before
you finish authoring them. The core `generate_client()` generates supplied
contracts without requiring every selected operation to have one.

## Inline YAML contracts

For a simple single-call test, use `contracts` instead of an RDS file:

```yaml
response_fixture: {id: item-1}
contracts:
  get_item:
    inputs: {item_id: item-1, language: en}
    request:
      method: GET
      path: /items/{item_id}
      path_params: {item_id: item-1}
      query: {language: en}
      body: null
      request_controls: {timeout: 30, max_retries: 0, retry_writes: false}
      server:
        diagnostic: Relative server URL requires a recorded origin or explicit base URL override
    result: {id: item-1}
```

A contract can override `response_fixture`. Inline single-call tests use
`test-<operation>.R`; RDS sequence tests use `test-contract-<operation>.R`.
Prefer the latter when a manual test already uses the simple name, multiple
helper calls matter, or results have R classes. Do not declare the same operation
in both inline and RDS contracts.

## Readable contract files

For reviewable call sequences, save the same structure as YAML or JSON and point
service `contracts_file` at it. For example,
`tests/testthat/fixtures/contracts.yml` can contain:

```yaml
GET /items/{item_id}:
  inputs: {item_id: item-1, language: en}
  calls:
    - helper: api_request
      arguments:
        method: GET
        path: /items/{item_id}
        path_params: {item_id: item-1}
        query: {language: en}
        body: null
        request_controls: {timeout: 30, max_retries: 0, retry_writes: false}
        server:
          diagnostic: Relative server URL requires a recorded origin or explicit base URL override
      response: {id: item-1}
  result: {id: item-1}
```

Set `contracts_file: tests/testthat/fixtures/contracts.yml` in `apis/default.yml`
in place of the RDS setting. The route key stays fixed if you rename `get_item`.
Generate, then run the client's tests as above; these expectations still need
independent review against the service contract.

## Candidate input fixtures are not independent expectations

`operation_fixtures()` chooses candidate inputs in the order **override ->
parameter/media example -> schema example -> default -> enum -> type fixture**. It checks supported constraints
and stops if the chosen candidate fails them; it does not silently try a lower
priority value. Examples never become public function defaults and are never
evaluated as R code. Required public arguments remain required.

Automatic selection uses the singular `example` field. Plural `examples`
collections require a reviewed override to select a member. Fixture creation also rejects empty query values
unless the parameter declares `allowEmptyValue: true`, as generated wrappers do.

The default fixture policy exercises optional inputs. Explicit `mode = "minimal"`
omits optional arguments, optional bodies, and optional object fields during
fallback synthesis. Explicit overrides and declared examples remain validated.
Each minimal input list records `attr(inputs, "omitted_inputs")`; report reduced
coverage separately. Omission may activate a wrapper default, so it does not
prove omission from the outgoing request. Explicit NULL, empty strings, FALSE,
and zero remain supplied values.

`read_operations()$fixture_diagnostics` reports type/enum contradictions with
source pointers and requiredness separately from parser blockers. Optional
contradictions remain visible in the default audit even when omission permits a
request. Fixture construction and localhost transport checks do not establish
live service acceptance.

```{r candidates}
operations <- specmill::read_operations(schema)$operations
candidate_inputs <- specmill::operation_fixtures(operations)
candidate_inputs$get_item
```

Review these values before using them against a service. They do not establish
expected helper calls or correct upstream results. `check_requests()` is a small
alternative for checking one zero-argument call against a capture function and
independent result; see its reference example.

## Declare cassette scenarios, gaps and unrecorded routes

A cassette scenario records one real response, then replays it offline
through the client's real wrapper, hooks and request helper. Declare what each
scenario covers first. Policy goes in the service YAML under `testing`:

```yaml
testing:
  file: tests/testthat/fixtures/testing.yml
  match: [method, uri]
  gaps:
    POST /items: {reason: 'Write endpoint; expectations pending', issue: '#300'}
  unrecorded:
    POST /refresh: {reason: Side effects on the live service}
```

- `file` holds scenarios and hook cases. It must sit under `tests/testthat/`,
  differ from `contracts_file`, and belong to one service.
- `match` lists the request parts a recording must match: `method`, `uri`,
  `host`, `path`, `query`, `body` or `body_json`. The default is
  `[method, uri]`. A scenario whose operation sends a body must add `body` or
  `body_json`. Header matching is not offered, because recordings compare all
  headers or none. Fixed contracts and local transport tests cover headers.
- `gaps` names selected routes that have no reviewed contract yet. A gap stays
  visible and never counts as a contract. It may name a route that specmill
  cannot generate.
- `unrecorded` names routes you have decided never to record. Routes without a
  scenario and without an entry are reported as not covered.

The data file declares scenarios. Each scenario will become one recording,
stored at `tests/testthat/_vcr/<service>/<scenario>.yml`:

```yaml
scenarios:
  get_item_basic:
    operation: GET /items/{item_id}       # route key, or the wrapper name
    represents: ['GET /items/{item_id}']  # routes with the same behavior
    inputs: {item_id: item-1}             # or `example: 1` for a docs example
hook_cases:
  trims_item_id:
    hook: normalize_item_id
    stage: pre_request
    state: {params: {item_id: ' abc '}}
    expect: {state: {params: {item_id: abc}}}
```

A scenario's default expectation is the reviewed type and shape of the result.
Add `result` for an exact value, or `checks` (`class`, `rows`, `names`,
`values` at a `path`) for the parts a reviewer verified. Routes in
`represents` are counted as represented, never as executed. Use the route key
for `operation`, so renaming a wrapper does not break the scenario.

`inspect_client()` checks the declarations against the selected operations.
It returns them under `testing`, with each route's status: `scenario`,
`represented`, `unrecorded` or `not_covered`:

```{r testing-declarations}
writeLines(c(
  'scenarios:',
  '  get_item_basic:',
  "    operation: GET /items/{item_id}",
  '    inputs: {item_id: item-1, language: en}'
), file.path(root, 'tests/testthat/fixtures/testing.yml'))
cat('testing: {file: tests/testthat/fixtures/testing.yml}\n',
    file = file.path(root, 'apis/default.yml'), append = TRUE)
declared <- specmill::inspect_client(root)$testing$testedclient
declared$routes
declared$scenarios$get_item_basic$cassette
```

### Generate, record and replay

Generation writes one `tests/testthat/test-scenario-<service>-<scenario>.R`
per scenario, a shared `tests/testthat/helper-scenario-replay.R`, and the
standard `tests/testthat.R` runner when the client has none. The client must
declare `httr2`, and `testthat`, `vcr`, `withr` and `yaml` (in `Suggests` is
enough); generation reports any that are missing and never edits
`DESCRIPTION`. A scenario needs `inputs`,
an `example`, or a wrapper with no required inputs.

Routine test runs only replay (`record = 'none'`). A missing or unmatched
recording fails without contacting the service. To record, set the real
credential and list the scenario as `<service>/<scenario>` in the client's
record variable, `<PACKAGE>_RECORD`:

```{r record, eval=FALSE}
withr::with_envvar(
  c(TESTEDCLIENT_KEY = 'your key', TESTEDCLIENT_RECORD = 'testedclient/get_item_basic'),
  testthat::test_local(root, filter = 'scenario', stop_on_failure = TRUE)
)
```

Recording writes the cassette and
`tests/testthat/_signatures/<service>/<scenario>.yml`, the result's class,
emptiness, column classes and nested element types. Review both before
committing them. Listing a scenario that already has a cassette replays it and
leaves its signature alone. The cassette stores credentials as `<<VARIABLE>>`
placeholders, including URL-encoded query values, and
`<scenario>.credentials` beside it lists the names (never the values) of the
credentials the recording used. Replay gives each of those a dummy value and
unsets the rest. Without a recording, replay stops and names the record
variable. Recording never
replaces an existing cassette: delete it to record again, and never re-record
just to make a failing expectation pass. Recording state-changing operations is
refused for now.

## Add the verification layer your change needs

| Layer | What to verify |
|---|---|
| Generation check | Committed output matches schema, policy, callbacks, and fixtures |
| Fixed helper contract | Successful wrapper result plus exact ordered helper calls |
| Hook tests | Validation, parameter changes, skip behavior, and post-processing |
| Cassette scenario | Real wrapper, hooks and helper replayed against a reviewed recording; result type and reviewed values |
| Local transport test | Final method, encoded URL, query/body placement, headers, media, and error decoding |
| Bounded live check | Current endpoint/authentication behavior using reviewed nonsecret input |

Use a local HTTP server or existing HTTP fixtures to test transport. Do not
re-record production traffic just to update generated tests. A live failure can
come from input, authentication, schema drift, generation, runtime code, or an
outage. Diagnose it before editing generated source or relaxing expectations.
